Calculate the electrical resistivity of the wire material in Ω·m.
Use the wire length L = 0.492 m.
Use the wire diameter d = 1.944 mm = 0.001944 m, so the radius r = d/2 = 0.000972 m.
Use the measured resistance R = 11.705 Ω.
Compute the circular cross-sectional area using the standard formula A = π(d/2)² = πd²/4 = π(0.000972 m)².
Compute the resistivity using ρ = R·A / L.
Do not use A = πd² with the diameter value directly, as that would overstate the area by a factor of four and yield an incorrect resistivity.
Report the final resistivity in Ω·m.
